title: PRESIDENT OF INDIA PRESENTS 72nd NATIONAL FILM AWARDS; CONFERS DADASAHEB PHALKE AWARD ON SHRI ANANT NAG
subtitle: INDIAN CINEMA EMBODIES THE DREAMS, TRADITIONS, AND STRUGGLES OF THE INDIAN PEOPLE, AS WELL AS THE POSSIBILITIES FOR THE FUTURE: PRESIDENT DROUPADI MURMU
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                22 SEP 2026 9:12PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The President of India, Smt Droupadi Murmu presented the 72nd National Film Awards at a function held at Ekta Nagar, Kevadia, Gujarat today (September 22, 2026). She also conferred the Dadasaheb Phalke Award for 2024 upon veteran actor Shri Anant Nag in recognition of his outstanding contribution to Indian cinema.
Speaking on the occasion, the President congratulated all the award winners who, through their exceptional talent and hard work have carved a niche for themselves at the national level. She expressed happiness that Shri Anant Nag has been honoured with the Dadasaheb Phalke Award. She said that his acting in films represents a synthesis of the finest elements of theatre and cinema. He is renowned for his natural, restrained and authentic performances. He sets an ideal example for future generations of artists.
The President said that the image of India is reflected in films across all languages and regions. Indian cinema embodies the dreams, traditions, and struggles of the Indian people, as well as the possibilities for the future. She was happy to note that the ceremony to honour outstanding films is being held on the premises of the Statue of Unity, near the Wall of Unity. She said that the occasion seemed to evoke the presence of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, the architect of India’s unity, as though he were himself blessing this festival celebrating the country’s cultural unity.
The President appreciated all the award-winning films. She said that the film ‘Article 370’ presents a vivid account of the serious challenges facing the country's unity and their solutions. The non-feature film ‘Bhangaar’ expresses unseen dimensions related to life and death, meaning and meaninglessness. ‘Swatantrya Veer Savarkar’ is an artistic tribute to the extraordinary life story of Veer Savarkar Ji. The film ‘Bhakshak’ raises societal awareness about the extremely serious issue of women's safety. National-level recognition of the Santhali film ‘Angen’ has provided encouragement to an outstanding film and it has also fostered cultural diversity and social inclusion.
The President commended the jury members for selecting films that address significant issues concerning society and the nation. She said that women's participation in every regional jury should be ensured. She underlined that in any field, a holistic human perspective can be formed by incorporating the viewpoint of women.
The President said that maintaining a sense of respect and sensitivity towards every member of the team should be an integral part of the film industry's work culture. She urged the key representatives of the creative economy to ensure that the workers, small-scale artists, assistants and strugglers receive due respect and social security.
The President said that the popular film artists possess immense potential to influence the people of the country, especially the youth. When successful film artists speak about the benefits of a disciplined lifestyle, millions of children and young people emulate them. She urged celebrities not to endorse products that are harmful to healt
h. She said that a true star is one who spreads light, not darkness.

title: Vice-President C. P. Radhakrishnan inaugurates 9th India International Water Week 2026 at Bharat Mandapam
subtitle:
Vice-President calls for judicious use, conservation and integrated management of water resources

“Jal Suraksha will lead to Jan Suraksha and Rashtra Suraksha”: Vice-President

Bharat's traditional wisdom provides valuable lessons for addressing today’s water challenges: Vice President

Small water-saving actions can serve the interest of humanity and the world: Vice-President
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                22 SEP 2026 2:40PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Vice-President of India, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan, today inaugurated the 9th India International Water Week (IIWW) 2026 at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi. The five-day event, being organised by the Ministry of Jal Shakti from September 22 to 26, is centred on the theme “Climate Resilient Water Management.”
Vice-President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan today inaugurated the 9th India International Water Week 2026 at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi, centred on the theme “Climate Resilient Water Management.”
Union Minister for Jal Shakti Shri C. R. Patil, MoS Shri V. Somanna & Shri Raj Bhushan…

— Vice-President of India (@VPIndia)
September 22, 2026
Addressing the gathering, the Vice-President said that water is the foundation of life and civilisations, stressing the need for its judicious use, conservation and effective management.
Recalling his childhood experiences in Tamil Nadu, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan said that he had personally witnessed water scarcity and remembered the importance attached to bringing potable water to people. “Saving water is of paramount importance for humanity and the globe,” he said.
The Vice-President recalled that more than two decades ago, he undertook a 19,000-km Ratha Yatra across Tamil Nadu, one of the objectives of which was to create awareness about river interlinking, water conservation and proper management of water resources. He said river interlinking could help address situations where some regions face floods while others experience drought.
Emphasising India’s civilisational connect with rivers, the Vice-President said Indian communities had developed rich traditions and practices for conserving, sharing and managing water over centuries. “Our traditional wisdom provides valuable lessons for addressing today’s water challenges,” he said.
The Vice-President noted that India accounts for about 2.4 per cent of the world’s land area and 18 per cent of its population, while possessing only about 4 per cent of global freshwater resources. He stressed that India’s water-use requirements cannot be compared with those of countries having greater water availability and smaller populations.
Calling for behavioural change, he urged citizens to adopt simple water-saving practices in their daily lives. “We can take a bath using two buckets or twenty buckets. The choice is ours. We can close the tap while brushing our teeth. These may appear to be small things, but within these small actions lies the interest of humanity and the world,” he said.
The Vice-President said climate change, rapid urbanisation and population growth were making water management increasingly complex. He stressed the need for an integrated approach encompassing river-basin management, groundwater recharge, rainwater harvesting and efficient irrigation.
The Vice-President highlighted the importance of cooperation among States in addressing water-sharing issues. Appreciating the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, he noted that 10 inter-State MoUs have been signed for water sharing.He appreciated the efforts of the Union Government, the Ministry of Jal Shakti and participating States in promoting cooperative solutions.He particularly highlighted the Kishau Multipurpose Project agreement among six States as an important example of inter-State cooperation.
Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan said that as India moves towards becoming a developed economy by 2047, efficient and sustainable water management will be critical. He recalled Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s call for “Jal Sanchay Jan Bhagidari” and urged citizens to make water conservation a mass movement.
He emphasised the need for greater water-use efficiency, recycling and reuse, particularly in view of the substantial demand for water from agriculture and the growing requirements of industry.He called for a shift from reactive to predictive and technology-enabled water management.
Calling for a multi-stakeholder and multi-dimensional approach, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan said water challenges cannot be addressed by any single institution, sector or State.He expressed confidence that the deliberations at India International Water Week-2026 would generate innovative technological, policy, socio-economic and environmental approaches for climate-resilient and integrated water management.
Urging all participants to share knowledge, build partnerships and commit themselves to saving and conserving water, the Vice-President said, “Jal Suraksha will lead to Jan Suraksha and Rashtra Suraksha.”
On the occasion, the Vice-President launched the Sustainable Urban River Management (SURM) Framework and AI/ML-driven Integrated Reservoir Sediment Management, marking important steps towards technology-enabled and climate-resilient water management.
Union Minister of Jal Shakti Shri C. R. Patil, Ministers of State for Jal Shakti Shri V. Somanna and Shri Raj Bhushan Choudhary, Secretaries of the Ministry of Jal Shakti Smt. Archana Varma and Shri Ashok Meena, Chairman, Central Water Commission, Shri Anupam Prasad, and delegates and experts from India and abroad were present on the occasion.

The programme will also feature the launch of Safety Dossiers on Gokshura (
Tribulus terrestris
) and Chandrasura (
Lepidium sativum
), Standard Treatment Guidelines (STGs) on Skin Disorders, and other initiatives and publications aimed at strengthening evidence, research, innovation and community wellbeing in Ayurveda.

The event will feature two scientific sessions. Scientific Session I, titled “Shashwatam to Vishwas - Ayurveda for a Healthier Tomorrow and the Road to 2047”, and Scientific Session II, titled “Integrating Therapies is needed to reduce NCD (Non-Communicable Diseases) Burden by 2027”.
Senior officials of the Ministry of Ayush, representatives of the Councils and various Ayush institutions will be present at the event. The celebrations will bring together key stakeholders from across the Ayurveda ecosystem, providing a platform for knowledge exchange and wider engagement.
The 11th Ayurveda Day celebrations will highlight the importance of evidence, research and innovation in strengthening Ayurveda and advancing community wellbeing. The nationwide and worldwide observance will reinforce the focus on Ayurveda for a Healthier Tomorrow.

title: Civil Aviation Minister Ram Mohan Naidu launches Challenge Mode for Aerodrome Development
subtitle: Next Phase of UDAN Takes Off with MoUs Signed with 21 States/UTs
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                22 SEP 2026 7:10PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Ministry of Civil Aviation today took a major step towards strengthening regional air connectivity across the country with the signing of 21 Memoranda of Understanding (MoUs) with States and Union Territories under the next phase of the UDAN (Ude Desh ka Aam Nagrik) Scheme. The MoUs mark a significant milestone in Centre–State/UT cooperation for the development of aviation infrastructure and expansion of air connectivity to underserved and unserved regions.
The ceremony, held at The Ashok, Chanakyapuri, New Delhi, was inaugurated by Shri Kinjarapu Ram Mohan Naidu, Minister of Civil Aviation, in the presence of Shri Murlidhar Mohol, Minister of State for Civil Aviation; Shri Samir Kumar Sinha, Secretary, Ministry of Civil Aviation; Shri Vipin Kumar, Chairman, Airports Authority of India (AAI), and senior officials of the Ministry.
"With these MoUs, Team Bharat is joining hands to take India's regional aviation to greater heights. Under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, Viksit Rajya is the foundation of Viksit Bharat, with every State as an equal partner in this journey," said Shri Ram Mohan Naidu Kinjarapu.
Talking about the impact of UDAN, the Minister added, "Since its launch, UDAN has operationalized 687 routes and 95 aerodromes, with more than 3.66 lakh flights carrying around 1.71 crore passengers. But the numbers that matter most to me are the numbers of impact, aviation-sector jobs have grown from around 3 million in 2014 to nearly 7.7 million today, with the potential to reach 25 million by 2040. Airports like Tezu in Arunachal Pradesh and Purnea in Bihar, once cut off from air connectivity by hundreds of kilometers, are today becoming drivers of regional prosperity”.
The launch of the next phase of UDAN builds on the inauguration by the Prime Minister at Jodhpur on 4
th
July 2026 and the UDAN Workshop held on 16
th
July 2026, which brought together civil aviation stakeholders to deliberate on the roadmap for the next phase of the scheme.
"Modified UDAN rests on four pillars; affordability for passengers, sustainability of operations, transparent Challenge Mode framework for projects and the promotion of indigenous manufacturing. Together, we are building an ecosystem towards the larger ambition of Made in India Civil aircraft. That is the direction in which this next phase of UDAN is taking us", Shri Ram Mohan Naidu added.
With today’s launch, the next phase of UDAN moves from policy and stakeholder consultations towards on-ground implementation, with a three-pronged focus on strengthening Centre–State/UT partnerships, creating aviation infrastructure and expanding regional air connectivity.
Speaking at the event, Minister of State for Civil Aviation Shri Murlidhar Mohol said, “Under the able leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, UDAN has come a long way since 2016 expanding regional and remote connectivity across the country. Now, with Modified UDAN, we are looking at 120 new destinations and 4 crore more passengers over the next ten years. With more than 20 States coming together, we are taking this journey forward and opening a new chapter in India’s civil aviation sector.”
A total of 21 MoUs were signed between the Ministry of Civil Aviation, participating States/UTs and the Airports Authority of India (AAI), the implementing agency under the UDAN Scheme. The MoUs establish a structured framework for coordinated action between the Centre, States/UTs and AAI for identification, development and operationalisation of aviation assets, aligned with the connectivity requirements and priorities of States and UTs.
The Civil Aviaation Minister also launched the Challenge Mode Portal for Aerodrome Development and released the Scheme Document for the next phase of UDAN Route Bidding.
Under the Challenge Mode, State Governments and UT Administrations will now be able to nominate airstrips and helipads for development under the next phase of UDAN through the dedicated portal. This will enable States/UTs to proactively identify locations with potential for aviation connectivity and facilitate the creation and upgradation of aviation infrastructure based on local requirements.
The route bidding round will invite airlines to bid for identified UDAN routes, enabling transparent and competitive selection of routes and operators. The process will facilitate the expansion of air services to unserved and underserved regions, improving accessibility and mobility and supporting wider economic activity, tourism, trade and employment.
The event also featured a technical session on the next phase of UDAN, covering the Challenge Mode for aerodrome development and the upcoming bidding round for selection of UDAN routes. The session provided an opportunity for States/UTs, AAI, airlines and other civil aviation stakeholders to deliberate on the implementation framework and way forward.
The next phase of UDAN seeks to build on the gains achieved under the scheme and further deepen the aviation ecosystem across the country, ensuring that the benefits of air connectivity and aviation infrastructure reach more regions, communities and citizens.

title: CCL’s Transformation Since 2014: From Higher Coal Production to Modern Mining, Sustainable Evacuation and Inclusive Development
subtitle: Central Coalfields Limited’s journey reflects a decade of expansion in production capacity, mechanisation, rail connectivity, technology adoption, renewable energy, financial strength and community development
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                22 SEP 2026 12:52PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Indian coal sector has undergone a significant transformation since 2014, driven by policy reforms, improved project clearances, infrastructure development, technology adoption, greater mechanisation and a sharper focus on efficiency and energy security. Central Coalfields Limited (CCL), a subsidiary of Coal India Limited operating in the coalfields of Jharkhand, has emerged as an important example of this transformation.
The scale of CCL’s operational transformation is reflected most clearly in its coal production. From
50.0 Million Tonnes (MT) in FY 2013-14
, CCL increased its production to
87.5 MT in FY 2024-25
, the highest-ever production in the history of the company. Thus, over the period since 2013-14, CCL increased its production by nearly 75%. A major feature of CCL’s transformation has been the creation of additional mining capacity through new and expansion projects. Mega mines such as
Amrapali (35 MTY), Magadh (51 MTY), Chandragupta OCP (15 MTY) and Kotre Basantpur Pachmo (5 MTY)
have been developed during this period. Capacities of existing mines such as
Karo, Konar and North Urimari
etc. have also been expanded. Several more new mines and expansion projects are in the pipeline and are expected to further augment CCL’s production capacity in the coming years.
The transportation of incremental coal to its consumers through sustainable and efficient modes has been another major challenge. The transformation of CCL is therefore equally visible in the area of coal evacuation and logistics. Recognising that higher production must be supported by efficient evacuation infrastructure, the company has progressively invested in railway connectivity, Coal Handling Plants (CHPs), silos, rapid loading systems and First Mile Connectivity (FMC) projects.
The
Tori-Shivpur rail corridor
, one of the most critical railway links for the North Karanpura coalfields, has been progressively strengthened. The three-line railway corridor has the capacity to transport around
100 MT of coal per annum
. To make coal transportation more sustainable and efficient, CCL is establishing CHPs and FMC projects. The
7.5 MTY North Urimari CHP
has already been commissioned. Major CHP projects under development include
Konar (5 MTY), KDH-Purnadih (7.5 MTY), Amrapali (25 MTY), Karo (7 MTY) and Magadh (51 MTY)
. These systems are designed to reduce dependence on road transportation, improve loading efficiency and facilitate direct rail evacuation.
Coking coal is critical for India’s steel sector, which continues to depend significantly on import. Recognising the strategic importance of import substitution, CCL has given a major thrust to increasing the availability of quality domestic washed coking coal, thereby contributing to foreign-exchange savings. The company is developing
five new coking coal washeries with an aggregate capacity of 14.50 million tonnes per year (MTY)
. Significant progress has been made in advancing these projects.
CCL is also embracing emerging technologies to transform the way its operations are monitored and managed. In line with the growing adoption of Artificial Intelligence (AI), the company has established an
AI-enabled Integrated Command and Control Centre (ICCC)
to strengthen security, surveillance and operational oversight across its command areas. The centre integrates modern technologies to facilitate real-time monitoring and more effective decision-making.
Another important dimension of CCL’s transformation is its increasing emphasis on renewable energy and energy conservation. CCL currently has
over 32 MW of installed solar capacity
, including three ground-mounted projects with a combined capacity
of 29 MW.
A mega
100 MW
solar power project is coming up in Giridih district along with a Battery Energy Storage System (BESS). These initiatives will increase the share of renewable energy in the company’s energy mix, reduce emissions and support its broader Net Zero commitment.
CCL is also making mining more sustainable through the adoption of modern and environment-friendly technologies. The company has adopted
blast-free technologies such as surface miners and continuous miners
, along with scientific restoration of overburden dumps, rainwater harvesting, plantation and mine reclamation measures. From
zero production through surface miners and continuous miners before 2014
, their share has now increased to
nearly 70%
. CCL is also utilising surplus mine water for the benefit of local communities, thereby converting a mining-related resource into an important instrument of community development.
CCL’s transformation has also been accompanied by a substantial strengthening of its financial position. Profit After Tax (PAT) increased from ₹808 crore in FY 2017-18 to ₹4,035 crore in FY 2024-25, while net worth increased from ₹3,816 crore to ₹16,464 crore during the same period.
The social dimension of CCL’s transformation is perhaps most visible through its CSR initiatives. CSR expenditure has evolved from programmes largely focused on basic infrastructure, drinking water, healthcare and education to larger, long-term interventions aimed at creating sustainable social assets and opportunities. In
FY 2025-26
, CCL reported total CSR expenditure of approximately
₹86 crore
, against a CSR target of about ₹74 crore.
Among CCL’s most distinctive CSR initiatives is
CCL Ke Lal & CCL Ki Laadli
. The flagship programme provides talented students from underprivileged backgrounds with free residential schooling and engineering entrance coaching, with
40 students—20 boys and 20 girls—selected every year
. The programme has enabled students from rural and mining-affected communities to pursue higher education at premier institutions such as
IITs, NITs
and other leading engineering institutions.
Similarly, the
Sports Academy at Khelgaon, Ranchi
, established through a partnership between CCL and the Government of Jharkhand, has emerged as another flagship intervention. Established using the infrastructure created for the
34th National Games
, the academy is operated through the Jharkhand State Sports Promotion Society. Over the years, it has provided structured opportunities in sports, along with education and life-skills support, to young athletes. Athletes from the academy are bringing national as well as international medals. This initiative as won National CSR award twice.
Today, CCL is therefore much more than a coal-producing organisation. Its transformation since 2014 represents a transition towards higher production, greater productivity, expanded mining capacity, mechanised coal evacuation, stronger rail connectivity, renewable-energy adoption, improved environmental management, financial strengthening and a broader social-development role.
CCL’s journey demonstrates that the transformation of a coal company cannot be measured merely in million tonnes of production. The increase from around 50 MT to 87.5 MT is only one part of the story. The larger transformation lies in creating new mining capacity, building modern evacuation infrastructure, integrating CHPs and rail systems, adopting renewable energy, improving productivity and environmental management, and investing in communities through initiatives such as CCL Ke Lal & CCL Ki Laadli and the Khelgaon Sports Academy.
As India continues to pursue energy security alongside economic growth and environmental responsibility, CCL’s experience since 2014 illustrates how a traditional mining enterprise can progressively transform itself into a modern, technology-enabled, infrastructure-oriented and socially responsive organisation, while continuing to play a vital role in meeting the country’s energy requirements.

title: Corporate Social Responsibility in Coal India Limited: A Journey from Community Welfare to Inclusive Growth
subtitle:
Coal India Limited’s CSR Expenditure Rises to Nearly Rs. 1,000 Crore Annually

CIL Spends Rs. 7,276 Crore on CSR Against Statutory Requirement of Rs. 5,795 Crore During FY 2014-15 to FY 2025-26
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                22 SEP 2026 12:07PM by PIB Delhi
content:
For a company whose operations touch some of the most resource-poor and tribal-dominated districts of India, the idea of giving back to the community is not new to Coal India Limited (CIL). Long before the Companies Act, 2013 made Corporate Social Responsibility a legal obligation for corporate India, CIL and its subsidiaries were already engaged in welfare activities in and around their mining areas under the Community Development (CD) Policy, 2005.
Under this earlier CD regime, subsidiaries supported villages within an
8 km radius
of mining operations through drinking water facilities, health camps, and small infrastructure works — meaningful interventions that fostered harmony with peripheral communities. In the three years leading up to the Act (FY 2011-12 to 2013-14), CIL's consolidated CD spend varied from
Rs. 82 cr. (FY 2011-12)
to
Rs. 409 cr
.
(FY 2013-14)
. The work being done was genuine and appreciated on the ground; what it lacked was a consistent, institutionalised framework to sustain and scale it year on year.
The Companies Act, 2013 and Section 135 changed this fundamentally. Companies were now required to spend a statutorily defined share of their average net profits on CSR, guided by Schedule VII themes and monitored by a Board-level CSR Committee. CIL built on this with its own policy architecture: at least 80% of annual CSR expenditure within a
25 km radius
of mines and establishments, prioritising Project Affected Areas, with the balance for state and national initiatives. As a natural consequence of this local-area focus,
more than 90% of CIL's CSR expenditure
continues to be incurred within coal-bearing states — keeping the benefit anchored where the impact of mining is felt most directly.
The results are visible in the numbers. CIL has not merely met its statutory obligation — it has exceeded it consistently, year after year. Cumulatively, from FY 2014-15 to FY 2025-26, CIL has spent
Rs. 7,276 crore
against a statutory requirement of
Rs. 5,795 crore
. What is more striking is the trajectory within this: annual expenditure, once closer to Rs. 500 cr., the yearly outlay now touches
almost Rs. 1,000 crore
— placing CIL among the largest corporate CSR spenders in the country.
This growth in scale has been matched by a growth in purpose, with CIL's CSR converging deliberately with national missions. It was the number one CPSE contributor to the Swachh Vidyalaya Abhiyan, completing over 50,000 toilets in government schools; it was among the earliest major contributors to the PM-CARES Fund and ran an extensive COVID-19 relief programme, from dedicated hospitals in Odisha and Chhattisgarh to oxygen plants under “Mission Praana Vayu.” Flagship interventions have given the programme a distinct identity of its own — the
NIRMAN
scheme rewarding
more than 1,300
UPSC aspirants from mining districts, the
Thalassemia Bal Sewa Yojana
enabling
more than 1,000
life-saving bone marrow transplants,
Nanha Sa Dil
screening
over 2 lakh children
and curing
over 1,700
of congenital heart disease, and the
Scholarship Schemes
with the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India reaching over 2,500 children. This has been matched by major healthcare and education infrastructure such as a
500-bed medical college and hospital at Angul
and a
cardiac care centre at Jharsuguda
, together worth Rs. 596 crore, now serve as tertiary-care hubs for their respective regions, while
Digital Vidya
has commissioned over 2,300 smart classrooms and 500 ICT/STEM labs in government schools, alongside a 5,000-seater state library under construction in Ranchi.
The reach extends well beyond health and education. Skilling and livelihood programmes — including Project PRAGATI, tribal women's poultry support, and plastic engineering and multi-skill training — have benefited
more than 48,000 people over the last four financial years
alone. The
Khelgaon Sports Academy
, run in partnership with the Government of Jharkhand, has produced over
1,800 medals
, including
15 at the international level
; and landmark public-interest works — from the centenary building at IIT (ISM) Dhanbad to the illumination of Kolkata's Howrah Bridge — have carried CIL's CSR footprint into premier institutions and national landmarks alike.
Taken together, these efforts have touched an estimated
3.56 crore lives, directly and indirectly
— with vulnerable groups including SC/ST communities, persons with disabilities, and women forming a significant share of the beneficiaries. This work has also meaningfully advanced India's own SDG commitments — health (SDG-3), education (SDG-4), gender equality (SDG-5), clean water and sanitation (SDG-6), and poverty alleviation (SDG-1).
None of this has happened by accident. CIL's CSR is governed by a structured output-outcome methodology — Annual Action Plans shaped by community needs, MoUs with defined deliverables and timelines, phase-wise fund release tied to milestones and Utilisation Certificates, and Impact Assessment Guidelines that make third-party evaluation mandatory for larger projects, layered atop internal, statutory, and CAG audit oversight. This architecture is now being strengthened at a sectoral level: on
8th September
, the
Ministry of Coal became the first Ministry of the Government of India to launch a sector-wide CSR framework
, aimed at bringing greater consistency, convergence, and accountability to CSR efforts across the coal PSUs.

title: Union Minister Shri Piyush Goyal Interacts with Industry Stakeholders on Ease of Doing Business, FTA Opportunities and Trade Reforms Workshop
subtitle:
Shri Goyal Calls for Strengthening Export Facilitation through Physical and Digital Mechanisms

Local Personnel Proposed to Strengthen Exporter Support at District and State Levels: Shri Goyal

Trade Connect platform envisaged to provide product-wise and HSN-code-wise information on tariffs, FTA opportunities and procedures
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                22 SEP 2026 9:36PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT) organised a stakeholder workshop on Ease of Doing Business, Free Trade Agreement opportunities and ongoing trade-related reforms at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi, today, followed by an interactive session with Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Shri Piyush Goyal and Minister of State for Commerce and Industry Shri Jitin Prasada.
During the interaction, Shri Goyal outlined the Government’s approach to strengthening export facilitation through physical and digital mechanisms. He said that instead of establishing separate offices of every department in every location, integrated Commerce and Industry offices are envisaged in major cities to provide businesses with a common point of access to multiple departments and agencies.
He had a frank interaction with industry representatives and directed officials to examine some of the suggestions made by industry.
The interaction was the first such interaction with a regional industry association.
The roller chain and industrial components manufacturing sector highlighted the positive impact of recent policy interventions in strengthening domestic manufacturing. The industry reported that measures including Quality Control Orders (QCOs), Minimum Import Price (MIP) provisions and higher import duties have supported significant growth in the sector, contributing to a 15-fold expansion, fresh investments of approximately ₹500 crore and the generation of around 5,000 new jobs. The industry appreciated these interventions for supporting domestic manufacturing capacity, encouraging investment and creating employment opportunities.
The Minister also announced a proposed network of approximately 1,000 trained local personnel, with knowledge of regional languages, to support exporters and prospective exporters at the district and State levels. These personnel would be trained and subsequently deployed to provide handholding support to businesses, including through industry chambers and regional associations.
Shri Goyal also informed participants about the Trade Connect platform being developed to provide exporters with product-wise and HSN-code-wise information, including destination-country tariffs, FTA opportunities and procedures for availing FTA benefits. The platform is also envisaged to use digital and AI-enabled tools to help businesses identify potential export opportunities and infrastructure gaps.
The workshop brought together representatives from industry associations, trade bodies and sectoral organisations, along with senior officials of DPIIT and the Department of Commerce. Discussions focused on ongoing EoDB reforms, trade facilitation measures, opportunities under India’s FTAs and challenges faced by industry in accessing markets and navigating regulatory and procedural requirements.
Presentations by DPIIT officials covered key initiatives relating to Startup India, Intellectual Property Rights (IPR), investment facilitation, the National Single Window System, industrial infrastructure and reforms relating to the Petroleum and Explosives Safety Organisation (PESO). The presentations highlighted measures relating to simplification and rationalisation of regulatory processes, digitalisation, reduction of compliance burden and improvement in approval and service delivery mechanisms.
A dedicated session on recent FTAs and trade facilitation reforms provided industry with an overview of opportunities and obligations arising from India’s trade agreements. The session also covered ongoing measures relating to digitalisation, documentation and simplification of trade-related processes and procedures.
Representatives from sectors including pharmaceuticals, textiles, man-made fibres, copper, automotive and engineering, air-conditioners and logistics, along with MSMEs and women entrepreneurs, raised issues relating to export competitiveness, trade documentation, regulatory processes, FTA utilisation, logistics, domestic supply chains, standards and testing infrastructure and regulatory certainty.
Industry representatives highlighted the need for greater interoperability between government systems and foreign trade platforms, including digital transmission and verification of Certificates of Origin under FTAs. The proposal to extend such electronic processes to other FTA partners was noted for examination. Industry also highlighted the need for further integration of the export cycle involving the Directorate General of Foreign Trade (DGFT), Customs, banks and other stakeholders.
The interaction also covered logistics and trade-process bottlenecks, including documentation backlogs and concerns relating to sea-freight costs. Sector-specific issues relating to rules of origin and imports, export quality and regulatory processes, import competition, testing and certification infrastructure, and regulatory certainty for MSMEs were also raised.
The importance of quality and adherence to international standards for strengthening India’s export credibility was also emphasised. Industry associations and Export Promotion Councils were encouraged to support awareness and compliance with destination-market standards and assist in identifying instances of fraudulent, substandard or non-compliant manufacturing for appropriate regulatory action.
The interaction reaffirmed the Government’s emphasis on Government–Industry partnership in addressing practical barriers to trade, strengthening domestic manufacturing and supply chains, and facilitating greater participation of Indian enterprises in global markets.
The workshop was part of the Government’s continuing efforts to strengthen the Ease of Doing Business framework, facilitate trade and enable Indian industry to effectively utilise opportunities arising from India’s expanding network of Free Trade Agreements.

title: Department of Telecommunications Hosts Third Investors’ Roundtable in Bengaluru for Telecom Manufacturing Zone Focusing on Investment, Innovation and Domestic Manufacturing
subtitle:
Union Minister of Communications Shri Jyotiraditya Scindia and Chief Minister of Madhya Pradesh Dr. Mohan Yadav Chair Investors Roundtable in Bengaluru

“24 companies already on board, propose to invest ₹5,500 crore in Gwalior Telecom Manufacturing Zone”: Union Minister Shri Jyotiraditya Scindia

Industry Engagement Focuses on Strengthening Domestic Telecom Manufacturing and Innovation Ecosystem; ~₹700 crores committed in Bengaluru Investor Roadshow for TMZ, Gwalior

The establishment of India’s first integrated Telecom Manufacturing Zone (TMZ) is in line with Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi's Vision of Aatmanirbhar Bharat and Make in India Initiative
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                22 SEP 2026 9:45PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Department of Telecommunications (DoT) organised its 3rd Investors’ Roundtable in Bengaluru today to engage with leading technology, telecom, semiconductor and electronics industry stakeholders on investment opportunities in India’s first integrated Telecom Manufacturing Zone (TMZ) coming up in Gwalior, Madhya Pradesh.
The roundtable, chaired by Shri Jyotiraditya M. Scindia, Union Minister of Communications and Development of North Eastern Region along with Dr. Mohan Yadav, Chief Minister of Madhya Pradesh brought together industry leaders and potential investors to deliberate on strengthening domestic telecom manufacturing capabilities, enhancing value addition, promoting research and development, encouraging innovation, supporting exports and developing a globally competitive telecom and electronics ecosystem.
Speaking on the occasion, Shri Jyotiraditya M. Scindia said, “The Telecom Manufacturing Zone is a powerful example of cooperative federalism in action. The Union Government and the Madhya Pradesh Government are working hand in hand, with the State putting in place incentives and subsidies of around ₹8,000 crore. This kind of collaborative approach creates the confidence for the private sector to invest, innovate and scale.”
The Union Minister further added, “India is now moving decisively from being a services-led nation to a product-led nation. In telecom, our three priorities are clear: increase domestic value addition, create intellectual property in India, and take Indian-designed and Indian-manufactured products to every corner of the world. We have seen India’s Atmanirbharta journey gather momentum across sectors, from semiconductors to aviation. The next frontier is telecom. Under Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s vision of Make in India, Make for India and Make for the World, we must now also Design in India and build products that compete globally”
The Union Minister also highlighted that, “Today’s Bengaluru roadshow marks the completion of Phase 1 of our investor outreach, with nearly 24 companies already on board. Our commitment is simple: if an investor has a query or faces an issue related to the TMZ, we will work to resolve it within 48 hours. We want to make Gwalior not just a manufacturing destination, but a destination where industry knows it has a responsive government partner.”
Dr. Mohan Yadav, Chief Minister of Madhya Pradesh, said, “Madhya Pradesh is emerging as a strong destination for investment across sectors, with immense potential backed by its strategic location and infrastructure. We are committed to creating a conducive ecosystem for industries, particularly in emerging technology and telecom sectors. I am confident that this partnership will bring new investments, generate employment and contribute to India’s journey towards becoming a global economic leader.”
The Bengaluru Investors’ Roundtable was part of the continued investor outreach by the Department of Telecommunications following the launch of the Telecom Manufacturing Zone initiative.
On 30
th
July 2026, Department of Telecommunications and the Government of Madhya Pradesh signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) at New Delhi, for establishment of India’s first Telecom Manufacturing Zone, Phase-I, at Gwalior. The MoU envisages a plug-and-play industrial cluster with integrated infrastructure for telecom and electronics manufacturing, research and development, innovation and allied activities. The Central Government is providing 100 per cent funding support of ₹493 crore for Phase-I, while the Government of Madhya Pradesh has provided approximately 170 acres of land free of cost along with investor incentives.
This was followed by the two Investors’ Roundtable in Delhi and Mumbai, where the industry assured investment commitments of ₹5,500 crore, with the potential to generate around 18,000 employment opportunities under the Telecom Manufacturing Zone.
The third Investors’ Roundtable, reflected  deep engagement of investors with the TMZ initiative, proposing investments between Rs. 700 crore to Rs. 800 crores after due consideration by their management. Several companies offered positive reviews for the  investments and will undertake site visits for evaluation.
The Telecom Manufacturing Zone initiative is aligned with the vision of Aatmanirbhar Bharat and Make in India, Make for the World, and is intended to catalyse investment, manufacturing, innovation and employment in the telecom and electronics sectors.
Before the Investors’ Roundtable, the Union Minister visited Qualcomm in Bengaluru, a leading technology and telecom company. During the industry visit, the Union Minister interacted with company leadership and senior representatives and discussed developments in telecom technologies, semiconductor capabilities, indigenous product development, research and innovation, and the scope for greater participation of technology companies in India’s telecom manufacturing ecosystem.
The industrial visit provided an opportunity to understand industry requirements and explore avenues for stronger Government-industry collaboration in areas including telecom equipment, semiconductor technologies, product design, research and development and next-generation communication technologies.
About Telecom Manufacturing Zone (TMZ), Gwalior
The proposed Telecom Manufacturing Zone (TMZ) in Gwalior is envisaged as an integrated plug-and-play industrial cluster for telecom manufacturing, R&D and innovation, covering mobile devices, optical fibre, telecom equipment and next-generation 5G/6G technologies. Under the recently signed MoU, the Central Government is providing 100% funding support of ₹493 crore for Phase-I, while the Government of Madhya Pradesh has provided approximately 170 acres of land free of cost along with various investor incentives.
A Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV) has been established for this purpose with 51% equity from the Government of Madhya Pradesh and 49% from the Department of Telecommunications.

title: TRAI releases Telecom Consumer Protection (Thirteenth Amendment) Regulations, 2026
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                22 SEP 2026 1:04PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI) today released the Telecom Consumer Protection (Thirteenth Amendment) Regulation, 2026.
TRAI had released the draft Telecom Consumer Protection (Thirteenth Amendment) Regulations (TCPR), 2026 for consultation on its website on 07.04.2026. Since the implementation of TCPR (Twelfth Amendment), 2024, the Authority observed the limitation in the availability of Voice-and-SMS-only Special Tariff Vouchers (STVs)  being offered by telecom service providers, where only a limited number of such STVs, concentrated on longer validities were being offered and making low-income consumers deprived of affordable shorter duration choices. In order to address this concern, the draft TCPR (Thirteenth Amendment) consultation was issued.
In response to the draft Amendment, a total of 1132 responses were received from stakeholders. An Open House Discussion (OHD) on the consultation paper was also held on 15.06.2026.
Based on the responses received from the stakeholders and on its own analysis, TRAI has finalised the Telecom Consumer Protection (Thirteenth Amendment) Regulation, 2026.
The salient feature of this amendment is to
mandate STVs with appropriate reduction in tariff, exclusively for Voice and SMS for:
validities corresponding to each validity period of thirty days and less than thirty days for STV being offered for Voice, SMS and data and;
validity renewable on the same date of every month and if the date of such renewal is not available in a month, the date of renewal shall be the last date of that month and;
at least one STV with validity more than (i) and (ii) above, corresponding to the validity period of STVs being offered for Voice, SMS and data.
The
Authority is of the view that such a tariff framework would sufficiently address consumer requirements.
This amended regulation will provide low-income consumers with more options, allowing them to recharge according to their requirements and financial capacity. Overall, it will improve choices for consumers preferring not to use STVs bundled with data.
The amendment has been placed on TRAI's website (
www.trai.gov.in
). For any clarification/information, Shri. Vijay Kumar, Advisor (F&EA) may be contacted at Tel No. 011-20907773 or at email ID:

Assam’s rich cultural traditions and heritage find a distinctive representation in the 8th edition of the PM Mementos e-Auction 2026, with a collection of mementos showcasing the State’s renowned handloom traditions, bamboo and cane craftsmanship, metalwork, traditional art and heritage architecture.
The Assam collection brings together objects that reflect both the everyday craftsmanship and the deeper cultural memory of the State. Alongside traditional crafts and artworks, the collection features mementos associated with important historical personalities, cultural institutions and significant moments in Assam’s history.
These mementos offer a glimpse into the skills, traditions and cultural practices that have been passed down through generations and continue to form an important part of Assam’s cultural identity.
The collection also includes representations of Assam’s heritage and cultural institutions, bringing together material traditions with the State’s historical and spiritual legacy. Among the notable mementos are artworks and commemorative pieces associated with Bir Chilarai, Bharat Ratna awardee Lokpriya Gopinath Bordoloi, Swargadeo Chaolung Sukapha and Mahapurush Srimanta Sankardeva.
The collection also includes a representation of the 1894 Patharughat Battle, recalling an important chapter in Assam’s history, along with representations of Bordua Satra and Swahid Smarak Khetra & Park.
The Assam mementos form part of the larger collection of 1,498 mementos offered in the 8th edition of the PM Mementos e-Auction.
The auction provides citizens, collectors, institutions, corporates and art and culture enthusiasts an opportunity to acquire mementos presented to the Prime Minister on various occasions. An accompanying exhibition at the National Gallery of Modern Art (NGMA), New Delhi, enables visitors to view the mementos and appreciate their artistic and cultural significance.
The PM Mementos e-Auction is organised by the Ministry of Culture through the National Gallery of Modern Art (NGMA), New Delhi. The funds raised through the auction are donated to the Namami Gange Programme, a national mission for the conservation and rejuvenation of the River Ganga.
The PM Mementos e-Auction 2026 is being conducted through the official portal:
https://pmmementos.gov.in/#/

Traditional Assamese Japi

Assamese Gamusa
– Several traditional Gamusas feature in the collection, showcasing the State’s renowned handloom heritage through intricate red and gold motifs and traditional Assamese designs.

– The collection includes several handcrafted brass Xorais, a traditional symbol of hospitality, respect and honour in Assamese culture, showcasing the State’s distinctive bell-metal craftsmanship.

title: SEMICON India 2026: From Silicon to Systems, India’s Semiconductor Journey on Display
subtitle: Exhibition Brought Together Industry, Academia, Start-ups and Policymakers, Showcasing India’s Expanding Capabilities Across the Semiconductor Value Chain
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                22 SEP 2026 12:10PM by PIB Delhi
content:
For three days, Yashobhoomi in New Delhi served as a showcase of India’s growing semiconductor capabilities. From chip design and advanced packaging to materials, equipment, artificial intelligence and high-performance computing,
SEMICON India 2026
brought together different parts of the semiconductor ecosystem under one roof.
Held from
17 to 19 September 2026
, the fifth edition of SEMICON India was organised around the theme
“Silicon to Systems: Building the Ecosystem”
. The event brought together the global semiconductor ecosystem, including industry leaders, policymakers, investors, academia and start-ups. The 2026 edition featured
more than 600 exhibiting companies
from various countries, along with a Start-up Pavilion, Workforce Development Pavilion, country and state pavilions, and a hackathon.
The exhibition provided a glimpse into how India’s semiconductor journey is expanding beyond chip design towards a broader ecosystem covering manufacturing, packaging, research, materials, talent and system-level applications.
From Chip Design to Advanced Computing
One of the key features of the exhibition was the range of indigenous semiconductor and computing capabilities on display.
C-DAC showcased its work in high-performance computing and AI, including the
AUM HPC-AI Processor
and the
RUDRA-AUM compute node
. These efforts reflect the growing focus on developing indigenous capabilities not only at the chip level but also across computing systems.
The exhibition also highlighted the broader movement towards indigenous processor design. India’s semiconductor ecosystem has increasingly seen domestic start-ups and institutions develop processor technologies, application-specific chips and system solutions for sectors ranging from telecommunications and automotive applications to artificial intelligence and surveillance.
Chips for Everyday Applications
The exhibition also offered visitors a look at how semiconductor technologies can move from laboratories and design centres into everyday products.
Indian semiconductor companies and start-ups showcased solutions for applications such as smart appliances, connectivity, surveillance, industrial systems, energy management and automotive technologies.
Among the companies highlighted in the Indian chip-design ecosystem is
Vervesemi Microelectronics
, which is developing semiconductor solutions for motor control, energy meters and data acquisition applications. Its work includes chips for applications such as consumer appliances, electric mobility and drones.
Such application-specific semiconductor products demonstrate the importance of indigenous chip design in building a wider electronics manufacturing ecosystem.
RISC-V: Building Indigenous Processor Capabilities
C-DAC’s indigenous 64-bit RISC-V processor strengthens India’s capabilities in homegrown processor design and semiconductor technologies. Based on the open RISC-V architecture, it supports high-performance computing and emerging digital applications. Its adoption in indigenous solutions demonstrates India’s growing expertise in developing advanced processor technologies for next-generation computing, connectivity and digital infrastructure.
InCore Semiconductors
showcased its work around indigenous
RISC-V processor IPs and SoC design automation tools
.
Its portfolio includes processor platforms designed for different levels of computing requirements, with applications spanning embedded systems and edge-AI use cases. InCore's processor IP has been silicon-proven across multiple customer chips and across technology nodes ranging from 180 nm to 16 nm.
The development of such processor technologies is an important component of the broader semiconductor design ecosystem, enabling Indian companies to develop products around domestically developed intellectual property.
Aheesa Technology has developed an indigenous internet connectivity device capable of delivering speeds of up to 1 Gbps, enabling Internet Service Providers (ISPs) to connect approximately 64 homes through a single Optical Line Terminal (OLT). The device runs on Vihan, a software platform developed entirely in India, and is powered by C-DAC’s 64-bit RISC-V processor. The solution represents a significant step towards strengthening India’s indigenous technology capabilities and advancing high-speed broadband connectivity through a fully Indian technology stack.
AI, Vision and Smart Surveillance
The growing convergence of semiconductors and artificial intelligence was another prominent feature of the exhibition.
Netrasemi
, an Indian semiconductor start-up, showcased its work in AI-capable
System-on-Chips (SoCs)
for applications including secure surveillance, smart sensors, robotics, drones and mobility.
The company has taped out an indigenously designed AI SoC for CCTV Surveillance in the 12 nm process node, integrating AI/ML accelerators, vision processing and video engines. Its technologies are aimed at applications requiring intelligent vision and edge processing.
The exhibition demonstrated how advances in semiconductor design are increasingly enabling applications in areas such as machine vision, smart infrastructure, autonomous systems and surveillance.
Semiconductor Innovation Across the Value Chain
The exhibition was not limited to chips alone. It reflected the larger ecosystem required to develop and manufacture semiconductor products.
From materials and equipment to testing, packaging and system integration, the displays highlighted the interconnected nature of the semiconductor value chain.
This broader approach is central to
Semicon 2.0
, approved by the Union Cabinet in July 2026 with an outlay of
₹1,27,500 crore
. The programme builds on the foundation laid by Semicon 1.0 and focuses on six strategic pillars -
design; machines and materials; more fabs; advanced packaging; research and development; and talent development
.
From Start-ups to Research Institutions
The Start-up Pavilion provided another window into India's emerging semiconductor design ecosystem.
The Government's Design Linked Incentive (DLI) Scheme has supported domestic chip-design projects across areas including video surveillance, drone detection, energy meters, microprocessors, satellite communications, broadband and IoT SoCs.
The
Chips to Startup (C2S) Programme
is also supporting the development of semiconductor design capabilities among students, researchers, institutions and start-ups. The programme is aimed at creating a larger pool of skilled chip designers and strengthening the country's electronic system design capabilities.
More than
one lakh engineers
from over
500 organisations
across the country, including
400 academic institutions and 100 start-ups
, have been onboarded by the ChipIN Centre under the C2S Programme and DLI Scheme. They have been provided access to advanced chip-design tools, chip-design and fabrication services, and specialised training. Together, these institutions and start-ups have developed
more than 300 chip designs
for fabrication at foundries in India and abroad and have recorded
over four crore hours
of chip-design tool usage. This unprecedented scale has helped create the largest centralised chip-design user base at the ChipIN Centre.
From Policy to Production
The exhibition
was held at a time when
India's semiconductor ecosystem was moving from foundational policy support towards manufacturing and commercial production.
Under the Semicon India Programme,
12 semiconductor projects have been approved across six states
, with investment commitments exceeding
₹1.64 lakh crore
. Three facilities have already commenced commercial production.
At SEMICON India 2026, the emphasis was therefore not only on what India aims to build, but also on capabilities that are already being developed across design, manufacturing, packaging and related technologies.
Building the Complete Ecosystem
The theme
“Silicon to Systems: Building the Ecosystem”
captures the changing scope of India's semiconductor ambitions.
The semiconductor ecosystem requires much more than the fabrication of individual chips. It brings together chip designers, fabs, packaging and testing facilities, equipment and materials suppliers, research institutions, start-ups, system companies and a skilled workforce.
SEMICON India 2026 brought these different elements together,
offering
a view of an ecosystem developing across the value chain and connecting indigenous innovation with global semiconductor opportunities.
From processor design and RISC-V technologies to AI-enabled SoCs, motor-control chips, advanced computing and semiconductor manufacturing, the exhibition showcased the many layers of India's semiconductor journey.
The story on display at Yashobhoomi was therefore not just about the chip. It was about everything that surrounds it:
the silicon, systems, people, research, manufacturing capabilities and partnerships
needed to build a complete semiconductor ecosystem.

Union Home Minister launched TVCs for anti-narcotics awareness, launched NCB website and laid foundation stone of new zonal complexes of NCB in Lucknow and Dehradun
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                22 SEP 2026 5:54PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah today inaugurated the 3rd National Conference of Anti-Narcotics Task Force (ANTF) Heads of States/UTs in New Delhi. On this occasion, the Union Home Minister launched Television Commercials (TVCs) to spread awareness against narcotic substances and laid the foundation stone of new zonal complexes of the Narcotics Control Bureau (NCB) in Lucknow and Dehradun. During the event, the best-performing ANTF of States and UTs were also honoured. In addition, the Union Home Minister launched the newly designed website of the NCB. In the two-day conference organised by the NCB, ANTF heads from 36 States and Union Territories, along with representatives of concerned government departments and other stakeholders, are participating.
In his address, Union Home Minister Shri Amit Shah said that under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, we have for the past five years been taking one step after another in an effort to achieve the difficult goal of a drug free India. He said that the time has now come to deliver a decisive blow against narcotics, which have become the most serious threat to the country and the world, and to achieve victory through collective efforts. Shri Shah said that by 31 December 2029, we will collectively succeed in uprooting the drug trade from India.
Shri Amit Shah said that in the past five years we have achieved success against several challenges such as terrorism in Kashmir, insurgency in the Northeast and the problem of Naxalism. The Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) with the cooperation of all the states, we have ended these major problems that have confronted the country for decades. He said that the fight against drugs is the most difficult of all battles, but we cannot abandon this fight. Shri Shah said that to build a
Viksit Bharat
by 2047, to save future generations and to connect the youth with India’s development, the only option before us is to make India drug-free. We will have to fight this problem unitedly and with passion, and we must achieve victory.
Union Home Minister said that the ‘Vision Document 2026-2029’ is like the Gita for all those involved in this fight. This Vision Document has been prepared with great effort after discussions with more than 35 departments. He said that we have prepared the complete roadmap after taking suggestions from all stakeholders, and it has been given to everyone with definite targets. Targets and timelines have also been fixed in it. The Home Minister said that it will also be reviewed after some time. Shri Shah added that the MHA or the NCB cannot do all this alone. We all have to fight this battle with top priority and complete dedication, and we have to win it as well.
Shri Amit Shah said that it should be our shared responsibility and resolve to end this menace of drugs that is hollowing out future generations. Our resolve should be that we will not allow even one gram of drugs to enter the country from anywhere in the world, nor will even one gram of drugs go from our country to the world. He said that we have prepared this roadmap with a resolve for the welfare of youth across the world. Shri Shah said that we will have to work for a drug-free India with sensitivity, with an understanding of its importance, and as the topmost priority. He said – Meet once the parents and siblings of even one young person afflicted by drugs. Until you meet them, intensity in this fight cannot arise in you. A weeping, wailing mother, a younger sister, and a boy who ranked in the top 10 in the Class 10 board examination is slowly moving towards death, while his helpless parents watch. There can be no greater sorrow than this for anyone, and for us too it is a national loss. A talented child who was going to contribute to India’s development in the days to come - his life is ending midway. There can be no greater loss than this for us and for the country.
Union Home Minister said that we have to fight the battle against drugs with clarity. He said that the focal points of this fight have already been identified, and a roadmap has also been prepared at the state level to take intelligence, investigation, financial action and prosecution in one direction. Shri Shah said that in the first ANTF conference we had created an institutional mechanism and strengthened it. In the second ANTF conference, we discussed capability, action and execution in order to convert that mechanism into action. Today, the third ANTF conference will convert this roadmap into a decisive battle.
Shri Amit Shah said that whatever we have done so far is not enough. Until the Principal of every school, the Patwari of the village, the PSI of the police station, the Director General of Police and the Chief Secretary of the state, and even the Home Secretary of the Government of India, work in one direction, we will not achieve success. He said that today’s conference is the most important because this time we will move forward towards complete victory by fixing
Target
,
Timeline
and
Accountability
.
Union Home Minister said that we now have to move from Meeting to Mission, from Reporting to Result, from Seizure to the dismantling of Networks, and from Case to Conviction. He said that until all departments of the state governments and the Government of India engage in this work, we cannot move forward.
Shri Amit Shah said that Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi has set the target of building a
Viksit Bharat
by August 15, 2047 before the 140 crore citizens of the country, when India will be at the forefront globally in every sector. He said that if we are to achieve this goal, we cannot do so with a youth power and future generation hollowed out by addiction. He stated that India is the youngest country in the world, which is why the threat is also the largest for us in the global context. This is our necessity because the health, skills, labour, and thinking capacity of the youth alone can lead the country to that goal, and drugs damage all four of these capacities.
Union Home Minister said that for emerging challenges such as synthetic drugs, diversion of precursor chemicals, new communication technologies, dark-net, drug markets, crypto, dead-drop delivery systems, and international drug networks, a team of officers who think 'out-of-the-box' should be constituted in every state, and success should be shared and implemented across the entire nation.
Shri Amit Shah stated that the Vision Document 2026–2029 rests on four pillars: Enforcement, intelligence & operations, Control of precursor & synthetic drugs, Demand & harm reduction, and Capacity building & coordination. Over 100 targets have been categorized across these four pillars. Under the target of registering 1 lakh
Nashamukt Mitras
outlined in the Vision Document, various ministries have registered 46,780
Nashamukt Mitras
so far, and they are already operational. To take this campaign to the grassroots level,
Nashamukt Mitras
will visit 10 lakh schools, colleges, and institutions across the country in the coming days to caution the youth and sensitize campus directors.
Shri Amit Shah said that today we are discussing converting the roadmap into results, and the most crucial element of the brainstorming taking place over these two days is compassion. Our goal should be to transform the ANTF into an ‘Anti-Narco Mission Command’, and State Chief Secretaries will need to adopt a different approach regarding manpower, technology, budget, and other resources. The Home Minister added that the Government of India is emphasizing technology and forensics in capacity building.
Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation stated that instead of maintaining a seizure-centric approach, we must move forward with the objective of dismantling entire networks. Our priority, along with backward-forward investigation, must also include financial investigation and tracing digital links. Our strike must hit the funds earned by drug dealers. Shri Shah said that cartels must be targeted at three levels: the entry point, the inter-state distribution system, and the local sales networks within districts. Further, districts will be categorized into three clusters: those where drugs are manufactured or enter the country, those serving as transportation corridors, and those where consumption takes place.
Union Home Minister stated that we must increase the utilization of PITNDPS, as there is a strong need for it in the country. A complete roadmap from investigation to conviction must be formulated in coordination with public prosecutors. A dedicated campaign must be launched to deport foreign accused present in India and blacklist them so they can never re-enter the country. Moreover, the fugitives who are supplying drugs to the country from abroad should be caught and brought before the Indian courts. By targeting borders and production centres, all loopholes must be plugged. Every ANTF should integrate the entire process of converting information to actionable intelligence into the work culture of their respective state police force. The Home Minister expressed confidence that we will succeed in this fight against drugs and emerge victorious.
Participation in this national conference will assist states, departments, and agencies under the 'Whole of Government Approach' to move forward with renewed resolve to effectively combat drug trafficking across the country over the next three years.
The deliberations held during the conference will help strengthen the effective enforcement of drug control laws and make the strategies adopted to protect the country's youth from drugs more impactful. This national event will provide an effective platform to bolster a future-ready partnership between the NCB and ANTFs of States and Union Territories to tackle drug abuse and fulfil the pledge of a
Nasha Mukt Bharat
.

The honour recognised his memorable performances and enduring contribution to Indian cinema over the decades.
Accepting the award with humility, Shri Anant Nag expressed gratitude for the people and experiences that shaped his journey.
Recalling his early years, Shri Anant Nag said that he grew up in an ashram before being sent to Mumbai, where he got an opportunity to act in a play. Theatre became the foundation of his career, and he went on to perform in around 50 plays before entering films. He later had the opportunity to work in films, including those made by acclaimed filmmaker Shyam Benegal.

He urged filmmakers to use cinema to promote natural farming, healthy lifestyles and environmental consciousness, and to strengthen values of love, brotherhood and national unity.
Gujarat Chief Minister
Shri Bhupendra PateI
welcomed the Hon’ble President and distinguished guests to Gujarat for the 72nd National Film Awards, describing the hosting of the ceremony at Ekta Nagar as a matter of pride for the State.
He highlighted cinema as a reflection of society, a carrier of culture and a powerful medium for connecting human emotions, with the potential to strengthen India’s global identity and soft power.
Highlighting Gujarat’s rich heritage, diverse landscapes and cultural traditions, he invited Indian and international filmmakers to choose Gujarat for filming and thanked the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting for bringing the prestigious ceremony to the State.
Union Minister for Information & Broadcasting Shri Ashwini Vaishnaw
expressed gratitude to the Hon’ble President for gracing the 72nd National Film Awards ceremony at Ekta Nagar, Kevadia, and congratulated all the award winners for their outstanding achievements in Indian cinema.
The Minister said that cinema is a team effort and that the National Film Awards recognise both those receiving awards and those working behind the scenes. He also lauded Dadasaheb Phalke Award recipient Shri Anant Nag for his immense contribution to Indian cinema.
Shri Ashwini Vaishnaw said that the focus of the National Film Awards is to take the ceremony to important tourist destinations across States and Union Territories, thereby promoting India’s rich cultural heritage and tourism. He called upon the states & union territories to pitch for tourist destinations as venues for the future editions of national film awards.
Highlighting the Indian Institute of Creative Technologies (IICT) as a new talent pool, he said that around 380 students have already enrolled in 13 courses, with the curriculum designed and driven by the industry. He further informed that the Hon’ble Prime Minister has approved 15,000 Creative Labs across the country, creating new opportunities for youth to learn emerging technologies and showcase India’s diverse culture.
The Minister called upon filmmakers and the entire film fraternity, with Shri Prasoon Joshi as Chairman of Prasar Bharati, to help identify, nurture and promote raw talent from small towns.
He reiterated that combined efforts of the Government and the creative fraternity can help unlock India’s immense creative potential and enable Indian talent to reach audiences across the world.
He also invited suggestions and ideas for WAVES 2027, to be held in October next year.
The Secretary, Ministry of Information & Broadcasting Shri Chanchal Kumar
, said that at the 72nd National Film Awards, 400 Feature Films across 34 languages and 161 Non-Feature Films across 24 languages were received, with 22 Feature Film and 23 Non-Feature Film awards conferred. He said that Indian cinema continues to grow as a powerful medium of cultural expression and global storytelling.
The Secretary said that holding the National Film Awards outside Delhi, at Ekta Nagar, is an important initiative inspired by Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel's vision and commitment to national unity, and that in the coming years, the ceremony is also envisaged to be held in other cities.
Celebrating Excellence: Stories, Performances and the Many Shades of Indian Cinema

Many Languages, One National Stage

From Garhwali and Tulu to Santhali, the evening brought diverse cinematic voices to one national platform reaffirming that every language adds a new story to India’s cinematic tapestry.
A Celebration of Indian Cinema
The 72nd National Film Awards brought together celebrated names, emerging voices, popular cinema and regional storytelling on one national stage.
