title: NHRC, India holds Statutory Full Commission Meeting in New Delhi
subtitle:
The meeting aimed to enhance synergy and cooperation among the Commissions for the promotion and protection of human rights

Chairing the meeting, Chairperson Justice V. Ramasubramanian says, the NHRC may explore extending support to other Commissions if lacking in machinery in the investigation of cases

Shares concerns over the lack of rehabilitation of mentally ill women engaged in begging, social security for PwDs and the denial of insurance coverage to them by insurance companies
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                22 SEP 2026 8:20PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The National Human Rights Commission (NHRC), India, organised a Statutory Full Commission meeting with representatives of all seven deemed members of the Commission in New Delhi today. The meeting aimed to enhance synergy and cooperation among the Commissions for the promotion and protection of human rights.
Chairing the meeting, Justice Shri V. Ramasubramanian, Chairperson, NHRC, India, emphasised the importance of collaborative functioning among the Commissions. He said that the Chairpersons of all the National Commissions are ex-officio Members of the NHRC and, therefore, are part of it. He said that together, the Commissions can undertake meaningful work for promoting and protecting the human rights of various sections of society.
Justice Ramasubramanian suggested appointing a Nodal Officer to coordinate among all the National Commissions. He said that the NHRC may explore extending support to other Commissions if lacking in machinery in the investigation of cases. In his concluding remarks, he also shared the concern over the lack of rehabilitation measures for mentally ill women engaged in begging, which requires attention. He noted that there is a sizeable population of persons with disabilities (PwDs) worldwide and stressed the need to examine policies intended for their welfare and identify gaps. The NHRC, India Chairperson expressed concern over the lack of social security for PwDs and the denial of insurance coverage by insurance companies. He also appreciated the suggestion for interfaith dialogue and coordinated research, particularly in overlapping areas.
The meeting discussed issues including an integrated approach towards protecting the rights of vulnerable and marginalised sections, identification of key areas for collaborative efforts, sharing of best practices and minimising duplication of cases. The participants emphasised the need for joint fact-finding efforts, research, awareness campaigns and outreach programmes.
Smt. Vijaya K. Rahatkar, Chairperson, National Commission for Women (NCW), highlighted the work of the NCW towards promoting and protecting women's rights and various programmes, including public hearings organised in different districts to hear their complaints. She said that, besides handling complaints, the NCW also focuses on research, awareness and outreach training programmes for the welfare of women. She added that the NCW has been organising anti-human trafficking campaigns in collaboration with Central Armed Police Forces and holding dialogues with youth on POSH, POCSO and cybercrime-related issues in collaboration with different institutions.
Smt. Kiran Umesh Mahalle, Member, National Commission for Backward Classes (NCBC), spoke about the problems faced by the beggar community, particularly those suffering from mental health issues. She expressed concern over mentally ill women being left by their families to beg on the roads. She suggested that the National Commissions may consider formulating a policy for their rehabilitation and recommending its implementation to the Government.
Shri S. Govindraj, Commissioner for Persons with Disabilities (CCPD) said that the CCPD has been focusing on reaching those who have remained unreached. He stressed the need for research into gaps in welfare measures for persons with disabilities, who he described as among the most vulnerable populations facing discrimination.
Dr. Sanjeev Sharma, Member Secretary, National Commission for Protection of Child Rights (NCPCR), highlighted the NCPCR's work on rescue and rehabilitation of children in a campaign mode. He said that over 8,000 children have been rescued and rehabilitated. He also underscored the need for capacity building and training. He said that the circulation of child sexual abuse material on social media platforms requires immediate attention. He suggested joint investigations and joint bench sittings of Statutory Commission members, besides strengthening State Commissions.
Shri Vivek Kumar Dewangan, Secretary, National Commission for Scheduled Castes (NCSC), said that the NCSC has set up an e-grievance monitoring portal, which has resulted in quicker redressal of grievances. He emphasised better coordination among the Statutory Commission members, collaboration on capacity building and awareness in educational institutions, joint studies on socio-economic indicators and joint action plans with measurable objectives.
Shri Suchindra Misra, Secretary, National Commission for Minorities (NCM), highlighted the importance of electronic grievance redressal systems and capacity building with support from the NHRC. He also stressed coordination with States to establish State Minority Commissions, noting that only 18 States have such Commissions so far. He further underscored the significance of coordinated research and complaint redressal, besides holding interfaith dialogues.
Shri Manohar N. Sukole, Deputy Secretary, National Commission for Scheduled Tribes (NCST), highlighting the importance of registering of
suomotu
cases besides the need for establishing grievance redressal platforms with real time tracking provisions and early warning systems identifying the recurring issues and overlapping matters requiring a more integrated approach among Statutory Commission Members.
Justice (Dr.) Bidyut Ranjan Sarangi, Member, NHRC, India said that the endeavour should be to work together to ensure that benefits reach the grassroots level. He said that while the Statutory Commission members work in different fields, their purpose is the same. He observed that SOPs can be effective if implemented properly and emphasised the need for adequate staff and infrastructure for all the Commissions to achieve their objectives.
Dr. Anupama Nilekar Chandra, DG (Inv) NHRC, India said that the Commission will be organising a training programme for investigation officers on the last Wednesday of each month beginning 30th September 2026. It will be further expanded over the course of time.
Earlier, setting the agenda for the meeting, Shri Piyush Goyal, Secretary General, NHRC, India, gave an overview of the country's unique institutional human rights protection framework. He emphasised that interactions among these institutions are useful in forming synergy and cooperation between different Commissions to protect the rights of vulnerable and disadvantaged communities including bonded labours, older persons and manual scavengers. The interactions can also help in paving the way forward for capacity building and sharing of best practices.
Shri Samir Kumar, Joint Secretary, NHRC, India, summarised the activities undertaken by the Commission over the last year.
The meeting concluded with a renewed commitment to collaborative efforts among the Commissions for the promotion and protection of human rights in India.

title: Department of Fertilizers Galvanizes Workforce with Special Creative & Participatory Initiatives Under ‘Swachhata Hi Seva’
subtitle:
Department Focuses on Employee Motivation through 'Kabaad Se Kala' and Idea-Sharing Drives

'Swachhata Hi Seva 2026': Department of Fertilizers Empowers Workforce to Champion Circular Economy
ministry: Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers :Department of Fertilizers
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                22 SEP 2026 5:54PM by PIB Delhi
content:
To streamline institutional initiatives and maximize on-ground impact during the nationwide
"Swachhata Hi Seva" (SHS) Campaign 2026
(being observed from September 17 to October 2, 2026), a comprehensive review and sensitization meeting was convened on September 22, 2026, at 11:00 AM under the chairmanship of the Senior Economic Advisor, Department of Fertilizers (DoF), Government of India, Shri Kuntal Sensarma.
The meeting witnessed wide institutional participation from key stakeholders across the sector, including officers of the Department of Fertilizers, representatives from the Fertilizer Industry Coordination Committee (FICC), and senior management executives, plant heads and designated Swachhata Nodal Officers from all Fertilizer PSUs, Cooperatives, and Joint Venture/Private Fertilizer Companies. The primary objective of the session was to evaluate the impact of the initial kick-off phase launched on September 17 and enforce unified alignment across administrative headquarters, manufacturing plants, and field formations to drive mass public and employee mobilization.
Focus on Five Core Thematic Pillars:
Following directions emerging from high-level inter-ministerial deliberations, the Chair emphasized the disciplined execution of 11 dated activities categorized under five foundational thematic pillars across all units and townships:
Swachhata Hi Seva:
Intensive, end-to-end cleaning and beautification drives across office premises, workstation cubicles, residential quarters, plants, and adjacent public areas, with special emphasis on sites of cultural, historical, and tourism importance.
Kabaad Se Kala (Art from Waste):
Creative initiatives encouraging personnel to repurpose office and industrial waste into functional, aesthetic, or artistic installations. Aimed at reducing carbon footprints, reusing resources, and institutionalizing circular-economy principles, departmental staff and PSU units have been invited to submit their innovative entries by September 28, 2026.
Khel & Khel Bhawana:
Organizing sports meets, fitness challenges, and community games—particularly on holidays—to foster health, discipline, teamwork, and an active lifestyle among employees, their families, and children.
Samvad:
Hosting interactive seminars, expert discussions, and awareness dialogues centred on water conservation, ecological balance, and sustainable environmental practices to drive institutional and personal behavioural change.
Gyan Yatra:
Conducting community awareness marches and rallies featuring informative placards to propagate core messages on sanitation, environmental stewardship, and civic responsibility, actively involving youth and local communities.
National Culmination: 'Ek Din, Ek Ghanta, Ek Saath' on October 1:
A critical directive was issued for the national mega-event scheduled for October 1, 2026. All fertilizer PSUs, cooperatives, industrial units, and field offices were instructed to ensure
100% workforce participation
for the voluntary cleanliness drive under the national banner
“Ek Din, Ek Ghanta, Ek Saath”
, dedicating one full hour of synchronized Shramdaan across all installations.
Employee Ideation and Periodic Safai Audits:
In line with earlier operational directives, senior officers of the Department are undertaking periodic
'Safai Audits'
to inspect sanitation standards and sustain cleanliness benchmarks. To promote participatory governance from the ground up, the Department continues to run the
'Ek Sujaav Swachhata Ki Or'
initiative, actively encouraging personnel to submit innovative, practical ideas to enhance workplace hygiene and administrative efficiency.
Real-Time Digital Monitoring & National Reporting:
To guarantee operational transparency and measurable outcomes, all participating entities were directed to upload high-resolution photographic evidence, short video documentation, and performance metrics on a daily basis directly onto the dedicated SHS-2026 Portal. Concurrently, units will maintain real-time reporting via the official institutional WhatsApp network. All uploaded field metrics will flow directly into the centralized repository for National-Level Performance Reporting, with comprehensive consolidated dossiers to be submitted by October 7, 2026.
The Department of Fertilizers reiterates that the sustained success of the Swachhata mission rests upon the dedication and active participation of its personnel, driving a cleaner, greener, and more responsive administrative environment.
